title: The Lighter Brief
overview: Big week in the US: the midterm results are rippling outward, from a judge pausing President Trump's planned arch in Washington to a wave of Democratic wins in North Carolina and a jittery day for tech stocks. Elsewhere, Interscope is heading to Brazil, Yung Miami is focusing on herself, a heart-scan study raises good questions about statins, and Sally Field turns 80.

stories.headline: Judge hits pause on Trump's planned D.C. arch
stories.summary: A federal planning commission approved President Trump's 250-foot 'triumphal arch' near Arlington National Cemetery on Thursday by an 8-4 vote. Less than two hours later, Judge Tanya Chutkan ordered a 14-day pause on construction while lawsuits from D.C., Virginia and a group of veterans move forward. Supporters call it a tribute to US history and veterans for the country's 250th anniversary, while opponents say it would block views of the cemetery and needs approval from Congress.
key_facts: The National Capital Planning Commission voted 8-4 after nearly nine hours of public comment.
Judge Chutkan's temporary restraining order bars construction for 14 days.
The arch would stand on Memorial Circle, between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.
Officials said work would run 20 hours a day for two to three years.
stories.why: It's a live test of how big new monuments get approved in the capital, and the courts will now weigh whether Congress needs to sign off.
